bullets.text: Afghan women report that their lives have become unrecognizable five years into Taliban rule, citing public floggings, job losses, and life-threatening barriers to healthcare.
An American missionary kidnapped in Niger nine months ago has been freed and is reportedly in good health under the care of US officials.

The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has spread to a sixth province, with a man dying in Bas-Uele after traveling from Haut-Uele, leading the WHO head to state the outbreak is on track to be the deadliest ever.
A trial project in Australia is allowing everyday locals to settle refugee families in their backyards, as communities nationwide embrace refugee integration amidst ongoing immigration debates.
The Nationals party is reportedly 'fighting very hard' to win Bendigo, following former Victorian premier Jacinta Allan's departure from politics.

Telstra has reported a profit and its CEO received a pay rise, despite remote areas of Australia experiencing ongoing struggles with service outages, which the company attributes to natural disasters.
Investors are returning to US stocks, driven by a strong earnings season and decreasing inflation, leading to a rebound in Wall Street.
Gold is approaching $4,400 an ounce as traders assess the Federal Reserve's interest-rate trajectory, following signs of economic cooling.
China is emerging as the dominant global oil power, with the Chinese Communist Party increasingly influencing decisions in the oil market.
